answer: To resist Sybil attacks, our economy enforces cryptographic stake burning where minting agent identities scales superlinearly: registering $k$ agents requires burning $O(k^2)$ tokens. This economic friction prevents any colluding cluster from turning into an isolated island of influence. Rather than letting adversaries perch safely on an exploit ledge, identity verification opens like a tiered lotus contract that demands exponential cost scaling, rendering mass entity replication economically ruinous.
